clinician.trajectory_summary: A previously healthy woman in her 40s presented 1 day after receiving AZD1222 (non-replicating vector SARS-CoV-2 vaccine) with acute onset of intense occipital headache and progressive lower limb weakness, becoming unable to walk more than 10 meters without support. Initial brain MRI on admission revealed multiple demyelinating lesions in juxtacortical and deep subcortical white matter, corpus callosum (including splenius), and cerebral peduncles on T2 FLAIR sequences. Two months after symptom onset, spinal cord MRI demonstrated longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) with significant signal alterations and cord swelling in the cervical and dorsal regions on T2 FSE imaging. Serology confirmed AQP4-IgG antibody positivity by cell-based assay. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed no alterations with negative oligoclonal bands. The patient met diagnostic criteria for NMO AQP4+ and was treated acutely with methylprednisolone 1000 mg/day for 5 days followed by intravenous immunoglobulin 400 mg/kg/day for 5 days. Maintenance therapy with tocilizumab (IL-6 inhibitor) was initiated. At 3-month follow-up, the patient demonstrated clinical improvement with recovery of motor and sensory functions, sensory level at T10, recovery of upper extremity strength, and trace muscle activation in the distal right lower extremity.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While brain white matter lesions can occur in MS, the presence of longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) with cord swelling, AQP4-IgG antibody positivity, and the clinical presentation with acute myelitis are more consistent with NMO spectrum disorder than typical MS. CSF oligoclonal bands were negative, which is less typical for MS.

While ADEM can present post-vaccination with multifocal demyelinating lesions, the presence of AQP4-IgG antibody positivity and longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis at 2 months post-onset are more consistent with NMO AQP4+ than ADEM, which typically has a monophasic course.
